para.text: One of the applications of 3D plotting is to create stereo images that produce realistic depth information. To achieve this each eye has to see a (slightly) different image. This can be done for example with a red/green stereo plot. In such a plot two images are drawn from different viewing positions, one in red and the other in green. With suitably coloured glasses each eye sees only one image, either the red one or the green one. By convention the left eye sees the red image, the right eye the green image.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: This system has limited possibility compared to other systems like the one using polarised light, for example no colour information can be generated. On the other hand, it can be constructed on every computer screen.

para.text: - No faces can be plotted. This is not a principle limitation of red/green stereo, but it is a result of the way XYGraph3D plots objects. As a result lighting and transparancy are disabled, and all objects are automatically plotted as open wire frames.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: - All lines are plotted as solid, as for dashed lines each line segment has to be in phase with the corresponding one in the other image, and this is practically impossible.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: - Text cannot be plotted in stereo. This is surprising, but it is a consequence of the fact the required plotting mode ‘

para.text: ’ is reset by Windows when a text is plotted (so don’t blame me). So all text is plotted ‘flat’; as this might spoil the stereo effect, labels and text at the frame can be disabled. An exception is the true 3D label plotting set by
where the labels and text are plotted as true 3D objects.

para.text: Occasionally a red/blue image is used instead of the original red/green, and sometimes red/green glasses work better with a more blueish green colour. Therefore you can set the green colour to any value.

para.text: In XYGraph3D the red/green image is not plotted efficiently. The best way would be to construct the individual red and green images separately in memory, and then construct the total image. However this limits the flexibility, so each image part is plotted immediately on the screen in both red and green. As each image is in fact plotted twice, and more overhead is required, plotting is much slower than for normal images and the metafiles are much larger.
